questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: RESPA was enacted by Congress in 1974 to address rising costs in real estate transactions. Lenders, brokers, and servicers must comply with its disclosure and anti-kickback provisions. What is the primary purpose of RESPA?

answers.text: To provide consumers disclosures about settlement costs and to prohibit kickbacks that increase those costs
To set maximum interest rates that lenders may charge on residential mortgages
To require lenders to make loans available in all geographic areas regardless of risk
To regulate the secondary mortgage market and securitization of mortgage-backed securities

explanations.a: Correct — RESPA's stated purpose under 12 USC 2601 is to give consumers settlement-cost disclosures and to eliminate kickbacks and unearned fees that inflate those costs.
explanations.b: Wrong — RESPA does not cap interest rates; rate ceilings are set by state usury laws or specific federal programs.
explanations.c: Wrong — that policy goal is associated with the Community Reinvestment Act, not RESPA.
explanations.d: Wrong — secondary-market activity is regulated by the SEC and federal housing agencies, not by RESPA.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Under Regulation X, classification as a mortgage broker matters because RESPA's anti-kickback rules attach to settlement service providers. The definition draws a line around persons who arrange but do not fund the loan. Under RESPA, a 'mortgage broker' is best defined as:

answers.text: Any title agent who arranges financing as part of closing services
Any individual employed by a depository institution to take loan applications
A person, other than an employee of a lender, who renders origination services and serves as an intermediary between a borrower and a lender
A person whose only role is processing approved loan files for a single lender

explanations.a: Wrong — title agents are settlement-service providers but are not mortgage brokers under Regulation X.
explanations.b: Wrong — an employee of a lender taking applications is acting as the lender, not as a broker.
explanations.c: Correct — Regulation X defines a mortgage broker as a person, other than an employee of the lender, who renders origination services and acts as an intermediary between borrower and lender.
explanations.d: Wrong — pure post-decision processing is not origination and does not by itself create broker status.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: RESPA applies to federally related mortgage loans on residential property. Whether RESPA disclosures and prohibitions apply depends on the property type and loan purpose. RESPA generally applies to a loan secured by:

answers.text: Commercial real estate of any type, regardless of borrower
One- to four-family residential real estate where the loan is federally related
Vacant land of more than 25 acres held for development
A loan extended exclusively for business or agricultural purposes

explanations.a: Wrong — pure commercial real estate is outside RESPA's residential focus.
explanations.b: Correct — Regulation X applies to federally related mortgage loans secured by 1-4 family residential real property.
explanations.c: Wrong — RESPA exempts loans on tracts of vacant land of 25 acres or more.
explanations.d: Wrong — business-purpose and agricultural-purpose loans are exempt under 12 CFR 1024.5(b).

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Section 8 of RESPA targets unearned fees that inflate the cost of settlement services. A common example is splitting a fee with a referral source who performed no actual work. Section 8 of RESPA prohibits:

answers.text: Charging a borrower a bona fide origination fee at closing
Listing actual costs incurred on the Closing Disclosure
Paying employees a salary plus a year-end performance bonus tied to overall company profits
Giving or accepting any thing of value for the referral of settlement service business involving a federally related mortgage loan

explanations.a: Wrong — bona fide fees for services actually performed are permitted under RESPA.
explanations.b: Wrong — accurate disclosure of actual settlement costs is required, not prohibited.
explanations.c: Wrong — bona fide salary and profit-based bonuses to employees are not Section 8 violations.
explanations.d: Correct — 12 USC 2607 prohibits giving or accepting fees, kickbacks, or things of value for referrals of settlement service business on federally related mortgage loans.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: When a lender establishes an escrow account at closing, RESPA requires an itemized statement showing the monthly escrow payment, projected disbursements, and any cushion. The deadline for delivery is set by Regulation X. The initial escrow account statement must be delivered no later than:

answers.text: 30 days after consummation, regardless of when the escrow account is established
45 days after the escrow account is established
The first scheduled mortgage payment date on the loan
The date of consummation, alongside the Closing Disclosure

explanations.a: Wrong — Regulation X ties the deadline to escrow-account establishment, not consummation.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1024.17(g) requires the initial escrow account statement within 45 days of establishment of the account.
explanations.c: Wrong — there is no rule tying delivery to the first payment date.
explanations.d: Wrong — same-day delivery is permitted but not required; the regulation grants up to 45 days.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: RESPA Section 9 protects a buyer's right to choose the title insurer in a residential purchase. The protection limits what a seller can demand as a sale condition. Section 9 of RESPA prohibits a seller from:

answers.text: Requiring, as a condition of sale, that the buyer purchase title insurance from a particular company
Paying any portion of the buyer's title insurance premium at closing
Negotiating the property sales price with the buyer's lender
Recommending any settlement service provider to the buyer

explanations.a: Correct — 12 USC 2608 makes it unlawful for a seller to require, as a condition of sale, that the buyer use a specified title insurer.
explanations.b: Wrong — sellers may pay all or part of the buyer's title insurance, and frequently do under purchase contracts.
explanations.c: Wrong — Section 9 addresses title-insurance steering, not price negotiations.
explanations.d: Wrong — recommending a provider is not the same as requiring its use; recommendations are not banned by Section 9.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Regulation X caps how much a lender may collect and hold in an escrow account beyond projected disbursements. The cushion absorbs disbursement variances without overcharging the borrower. The maximum escrow cushion permitted under Section 10 of RESPA is:

answers.text: Equal to one full year of escrow disbursements
One-twelfth of the total annual escrow disbursements
An amount the loan contract specifies, with no federal cap
One-sixth of the total annual escrow disbursements, equal to two months of escrow payments

explanations.a: Wrong — a full year would be five times what 12 CFR 1024.17(c) allows.
explanations.b: Wrong — one-twelfth is one month, less than the regulatory cap.
explanations.c: Wrong — the federal cap controls regardless of contractual language.
explanations.d: Correct — 12 CFR 1024.17(c)(1) caps the cushion at one-sixth of annual disbursements (about two months).

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Several transaction types fall outside RESPA's coverage even when secured by real estate. The exemptions narrow the universe of loans requiring RESPA disclosures. Which of the following is exempt from RESPA?

answers.text: A 30-year fixed-rate purchase loan on a single-family principal residence
A refinance of an existing first lien on an owner-occupied duplex
A loan extended primarily for a business, commercial, or agricultural purpose
An FHA-insured loan on an owner-occupied 1-4 unit dwelling

explanations.a: Wrong — owner-occupied 1-4 family purchase loans are core RESPA-covered transactions.
explanations.b: Wrong — refinancing a 1-4 family lien is covered.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1024.5(b)(2) exempts loans extended primarily for business, commercial, or agricultural purposes.
explanations.d: Wrong — FHA-insured 1-4 family residential loans are federally related and covered.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: When loan servicing is transferred, both the transferor and the transferee servicer have notice obligations to the borrower. The notice tells the borrower where to send future payments and who to contact about the loan. The transferor servicer must send notice of a servicing transfer to the borrower:

answers.text: At least 15 days before the effective date of transfer
Within 30 days after the effective date of transfer
At least 60 days before the effective date of transfer
Only if the borrower asks for the information in writing

explanations.a: Correct — 12 CFR 1024.33(b)(3) requires the transferor to provide notice at least 15 days before the effective date of transfer.
explanations.b: Wrong — that timing is past the deadline; the transferor must give notice before the transfer.
explanations.c: Wrong — 60 days is not the rule and exceeds what the regulation requires.
explanations.d: Wrong — the notice is mandatory, not conditional on a borrower request.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Regulation X imposes pre-foreclosure restrictions on servicers of mortgage loans secured by a borrower's principal residence. The rule limits when the first foreclosure-related filing may occur. A servicer generally may not make the first notice or filing required for foreclosure unless the borrower's mortgage obligation is more than:

answers.text: 30 days delinquent and unresponsive to early-intervention contact
60 days delinquent
120 days delinquent
180 days delinquent

explanations.a: Wrong — 30 days triggers early-intervention duties, not the right to start foreclosure.
explanations.b: Wrong — 60 days does not lift the foreclosure-filing prohibition.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1024.41(f) generally bars the first foreclosure notice or filing until the borrower is more than 120 days delinquent.
explanations.d: Wrong — 180 days is not the federal threshold for the first filing under Regulation X.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: After the initial escrow statement, RESPA requires servicers to provide a recurring statement summarizing escrow activity. The statement reconciles deposits, disbursements, and balance for the prior period. The annual escrow account statement must be delivered to the borrower:

answers.text: Every 6 months from the initial escrow statement
At least once during each escrow account computation year
Every 30 days following any escrow disbursement
Only when the borrower requests it in writing

explanations.a: Wrong — the regulation requires an annual, not semi-annual, statement.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1024.17(i) requires an annual escrow account statement within 30 days after the end of each computation year.
explanations.c: Wrong — disbursement events do not each trigger a statement.
explanations.d: Wrong — the statement is automatic, not request-based.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: When a referring party has an ownership interest in a settlement service provider, RESPA requires a written affiliated business arrangement disclosure. The disclosure protects the borrower's right to shop. An affiliated business arrangement disclosure must inform the consumer of all of the following EXCEPT:

answers.text: The nature of the relationship between the provider and the referring party
An estimated charge or range of charges generally made by the affiliated provider
That the consumer is not required to use the affiliated provider
That a kickback has been paid to the referring party in connection with the referral

explanations.a: Wrong — the ABA disclosure must describe the nature of the affiliated relationship.
explanations.b: Wrong — an estimated charge or range of charges is a required ABA disclosure element.
explanations.c: Wrong — the disclosure must affirmatively tell the consumer they are free to shop elsewhere.
explanations.d: Correct — RESPA's safe harbor permits ABAs without kickbacks; an admission of a kickback would itself describe a Section 8 violation.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: ECOA forbids creditors from discriminating against applicants on specified bases. Regulation B implements ECOA's protections in consumer credit transactions. Which of the following is a prohibited basis for discrimination under ECOA?

answers.text: Credit score and length of credit history alone
Race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age, or receipt of public assistance
Stable employment and verified income
Debt-to-income ratio and loan-to-value ratio

explanations.a: Wrong — credit score and history are permitted underwriting factors.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1002.4 lists the protected bases including age, marital status, public assistance income, and exercise of CCPA rights.
explanations.c: Wrong — employment and income may lawfully be considered.
explanations.d: Wrong — DTI and LTV are core underwriting metrics, not prohibited bases.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: After a creditor takes action on a completed application, ECOA imposes a notification deadline. The rule applies whether the application is approved, denied, withdrawn, or counter-offered. A creditor must notify an applicant of action taken on a completed application within:

answers.text: 15 days of receipt of the application
60 days of receipt of the completed application
90 days of consummation
30 days of receipt of the completed application

explanations.a: Wrong — 15 days is shorter than the regulation requires.
explanations.b: Wrong — 60 days exceeds the regulatory deadline.
explanations.c: Wrong — the deadline runs from receipt of a completed application, not consummation.
explanations.d: Correct — 12 CFR 1002.9(a)(1) requires action-taken notification within 30 days after receiving a completed application.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Under Regulation B, the term 'elderly' has a specific definition for purposes of evaluating creditworthiness. Age may be considered in narrow ways, such as for empirical credit-scoring systems. For ECOA purposes, an applicant is considered 'elderly' if the applicant is age:

answers.text: 62 or older
65 or older
60 or older
55 or older

explanations.a: Correct — 12 CFR 1002.2(o) defines 'elderly' as age 62 or older.
explanations.b: Wrong — Regulation B uses 62, not 65.
explanations.c: Wrong — 60 is below the regulatory threshold.
explanations.d: Wrong — 55 does not meet the elderly definition under Regulation B.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: On a face-to-face residential mortgage application, the MLO requests government monitoring information for ethnicity, race, and sex. The applicant declines to provide it. What must the MLO do?

answers.text: Refuse to take the application until the applicant provides the information
Leave the monitoring section entirely blank and submit the file
Note the applicant's refusal and complete the section based on visual observation and surname
Mark the section 'not applicable' and proceed to underwriting

explanations.a: Wrong — the application cannot be refused for failure to provide demographic information.
explanations.b: Wrong — leaving the section blank does not satisfy Regulation B's monitoring duty in face-to-face apps.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1002.13(c) requires the MLO to note the refusal and record the information based on visual observation or surname for face-to-face applications.
explanations.d: Wrong — 'not applicable' is not the prescribed response when the data must be collected.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Regulation B limits when a creditor may require an additional party on a credit obligation. The rule protects creditworthy applicants from being forced to bring in a spouse. A creditor may NOT require a spouse to sign the credit instrument when:

answers.text: The applicant lives in a community property state
The loan is secured by jointly owned real estate
The applicant qualifies independently for the requested credit on the requested terms
The applicant earns less than the spouse

explanations.a: Wrong — community property rules may justify a spousal signature on the security instrument, but not as a co-signer for credit.
explanations.b: Wrong — requiring a signature on the security instrument because of joint ownership differs from requiring a co-signer; the latter is barred when the applicant qualifies alone.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1002.7(d) prohibits requiring a spouse's signature when the applicant qualifies independently under the creditor's standards.
explanations.d: Wrong — relative income is not a basis for requiring a spousal co-signer.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: An applicant volunteers that part of their income consists of alimony and child support. Under Regulation B, how should the creditor treat this income?

answers.text: Exclude it from the qualifying calculation
Consider it to the extent the applicant chooses to disclose it and it is likely to continue
Verify the marital status of the payer before counting it
Discount it by at least 50% to be conservative

explanations.a: Wrong — categorical exclusion of disclosed alimony or child support violates Regulation B.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1002.6(b)(5) allows the creditor to consider these payments to the extent they are likely to be consistently made.
explanations.c: Wrong — the payer's marital status is not the qualifying test; consistency of receipt is.
explanations.d: Wrong — there is no required across-the-board haircut on these income types.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Regulation B defines 'adverse action' broadly to capture creditor decisions that affect the applicant's ability to obtain credit on the requested terms. The definition triggers specific notification duties. Which of the following is adverse action under Regulation B?

answers.text: Receiving a completed application and beginning underwriting
Approving a loan exactly as the borrower applied for it
Sending a status update to the applicant during processing
A counter-offer that the applicant does not accept

explanations.a: Wrong — beginning underwriting is not an action on the application.
explanations.b: Wrong — approval as applied for is favorable action, not adverse.
explanations.c: Wrong — interim status updates are not credit decisions.
explanations.d: Correct — 12 CFR 1002.2(c) treats an unaccepted counter-offer as an adverse action triggering notification.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: On a residential mortgage application secured by a 1-4 family principal dwelling, Regulation B requires requesting certain monitoring information. The data is collected for fair-lending oversight. Which of the following must be requested on the application?

answers.text: Ethnicity, race, sex, marital status, and age
The applicant's social media profiles
The applicant's voter registration status
The applicant's religion and political affiliation

explanations.a: Correct — 12 CFR 1002.13 requires this monitoring information on dwelling-secured residential mortgage applications.
explanations.b: Wrong — social media identifiers are not collected under Regulation B.
explanations.c: Wrong — voter registration is not a Regulation B item.
explanations.d: Wrong — religion is a prohibited basis and is not collected; political affiliation is irrelevant.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Regulation B prohibits discrimination based on the protected source of an applicant's income. Public assistance income is one such protected category, though the creditor may still verify amount and likely continuance. A creditor may NOT do which of the following?

answers.text: Verify the amount and likely continuance of an applicant's public assistance income
Require documentation of all income sources, including public assistance
Refuse to consider income from a public assistance program in evaluating creditworthiness
Consider the applicant's overall debt-to-income ratio after counting all eligible income

explanations.a: Wrong — verifying amount and continuance is permitted under Regulation B.
explanations.b: Wrong — uniform verification of all income types is permitted.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1002.6(b)(2) prohibits discounting or refusing to consider income because it derives from a public assistance program.
explanations.d: Wrong — DTI analysis is a standard, permitted underwriting practice.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: After denying a residential mortgage application, the creditor must provide the applicant a written statement under Regulation B. The notice must give the applicant either the reasons or the right to obtain them. The adverse action notice must:

answers.text: State the specific principal reasons for the action or disclose the applicant's right to request the reasons within 60 days
Identify the specific credit-scoring model used and disclose its proprietary algorithm
Include a copy of the appraisal, regardless of who paid for it
Recommend an alternative lender that may approve the loan

explanations.a: Correct — 12 CFR 1002.9(a)(2) requires either a statement of specific principal reasons or notice of the right to request them within 60 days.
explanations.b: Wrong — proprietary algorithms are not required to be disclosed; specific reasons are.
explanations.c: Wrong — appraisal copies are required by ECOA's appraisal-copy rule, but not as part of the adverse action notice content.
explanations.d: Wrong — recommending alternative lenders is not a Regulation B requirement.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Regulation B permits a creditor to ask certain questions during the application process even though similar questions on other bases are forbidden. The permissible inquiries serve underwriting or compliance purposes. Which of the following inquiries is PERMITTED under Regulation B?

answers.text: Whether the applicant intends to have or rear children
The applicant's birth control practices
The race of the applicant's spouse where the spouse is not on the application
Whether the applicant receives alimony, child support, or separate maintenance that the applicant wishes to be considered

explanations.a: Wrong — childbearing inquiries are prohibited under 12 CFR 1002.5(d).
explanations.b: Wrong — questions about birth control are prohibited.
explanations.c: Wrong — race of a non-applicant spouse cannot be inquired about for credit purposes.
explanations.d: Correct — Regulation B 1002.5(c)(2) permits asking whether the applicant wishes to have such income considered, with required disclosure that disclosure is optional.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Regulation B forbids age-based discrimination but allows creditors to consider age in narrow circumstances. One key allowance is that the applicant must be old enough to enter into a binding contract. Under Regulation B, age may be considered when the applicant:

answers.text: Is younger than 25 to assess credit history depth
Has not reached the age of majority under applicable state law required to contract
Is older than 55 to assess retirement income reliability
Is at least 18 years old, regardless of state law

explanations.a: Wrong — age may not be used to treat young creditworthy applicants worse on the basis of age.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1002.6(b)(2) permits age use to determine whether the applicant has capacity to contract under state law.
explanations.c: Wrong — age cannot be used to discriminate against older applicants on retirement-income assumptions.
explanations.d: Wrong — capacity is set by state law, which may differ from a uniform 18-year-old rule.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: TILA was enacted to standardize how credit cost is disclosed so consumers can compare loan offers. Regulation Z implements TILA across consumer credit, including residential mortgages. The primary purpose of the Truth in Lending Act is to:

answers.text: Cap interest rates on consumer loans nationwide
Require all creditors to use a single standardized loan note
Establish national underwriting guidelines for residential mortgages
Promote informed use of consumer credit through meaningful disclosure of credit terms

explanations.a: Wrong — TILA does not impose national interest-rate ceilings.
explanations.b: Wrong — TILA standardizes disclosures, not loan instruments.
explanations.c: Wrong — underwriting standards come from other rules, including ATR/QM under Reg Z but not from TILA's purpose statement.
explanations.d: Correct — 15 USC 1601 sets TILA's purpose as ensuring meaningful disclosure of credit terms so consumers can compare credit offers.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Regulation Z defines APR as a key disclosure on residential mortgage loans. The figure helps consumers compare offers across lenders. The annual percentage rate (APR) represents:

answers.text: The cost of credit to the borrower expressed as a yearly rate that includes finance charges
The note rate on the loan, expressed as a yearly percentage
The interest rate after the first scheduled adjustment on an ARM
The yield the lender expects after selling the loan in the secondary market

explanations.a: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.22 defines APR as the cost of credit as a yearly rate, including finance charges, not just the note rate.
explanations.b: Wrong — the note rate is the contract interest rate; APR is broader.
explanations.c: Wrong — that is the first adjusted rate on an ARM, not APR.
explanations.d: Wrong — secondary-market yield is unrelated to the consumer-disclosure APR.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Regulation Z defines the 'finance charge' to capture costs that are part of the price of credit. The figure feeds into the APR and the consumer's total cost of borrowing. The finance charge is best described as:

answers.text: Only the interest paid over the life of the loan
The principal balance plus all interest scheduled to accrue
The sum of all charges payable directly or indirectly by the consumer and imposed as an incident to the extension of credit
Only third-party fees collected at closing, such as recording charges

explanations.a: Wrong — interest alone understates the finance charge under Regulation Z.
explanations.b: Wrong — the finance charge does not include principal.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.4(a) defines finance charge as the sum of all charges payable by the consumer imposed as an incident to credit.
explanations.d: Wrong — recording charges are typically excluded under 1026.4(e).

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: TILA's coverage rules determine when Regulation Z disclosures apply to a transaction. Coverage turns on the purpose, the borrower, and the loan structure. TILA generally applies to:

answers.text: Loans extended to corporations for business operations
Consumer credit extended by a creditor that is subject to a finance charge or payable in more than four installments
Credit extended to government agencies for public projects
Agricultural loans secured by farmland of any size

explanations.a: Wrong — credit to organizations and businesses is generally exempt under Regulation Z.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.1(c) and 1026.2 limit TILA to consumer credit subject to a finance charge or payable in more than four installments.
explanations.c: Wrong — government-purpose extensions of credit are exempt.
explanations.d: Wrong — agricultural loans are exempt under Regulation Z.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: For certain consumer credit transactions secured by the borrower's principal dwelling, TILA provides a right to cancel. The window protects the consumer's home from rushed financing decisions. The right of rescission generally lasts:

answers.text: Until midnight of the third business day following the later of consummation, delivery of material TILA disclosures, or delivery of the notice of right to rescind
Until midnight of the seventh business day following consummation
Until midnight of the tenth calendar day following the loan estimate
For 30 days following consummation

explanations.a: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.23(a)(3) measures the rescission period from the latest of these three events.
explanations.b: Wrong — 7 days is not the rescission window under Regulation Z.
explanations.c: Wrong — rescission runs from consummation, not from the LE.
explanations.d: Wrong — 30 days is far longer than Regulation Z provides.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: The right of rescission attaches to specific transaction types under Regulation Z. Identifying when it applies prevents missed cancellation deadlines. The right of rescission applies to:

answers.text: A purchase money mortgage on a primary residence
A construction-only loan with no permanent financing on a vacant lot
A loan secured by a second home used only for vacations
A refinance with a new creditor on the borrower's principal dwelling

explanations.a: Wrong — purchase money loans on a principal dwelling are excluded from rescission.
explanations.b: Wrong — construction loans on vacant lots without principal-dwelling status are not subject to rescission.
explanations.c: Wrong — second homes are not principal dwellings; rescission attaches only to the principal dwelling.
explanations.d: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.23 applies the right of rescission to refinances with a new creditor secured by the consumer's principal dwelling.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Some real-estate-secured transactions are excluded from TILA's right of rescission. Knowing the exclusions prevents incorrect disclosures. The right of rescission does NOT apply to:

answers.text: A new second mortgage with a new creditor on a principal residence
A residential mortgage transaction used to acquire or build the consumer's principal dwelling
A cash-out refinance on the borrower's principal residence
A HELOC on the borrower's principal residence

explanations.a: Wrong — a new junior mortgage with a new creditor on the principal dwelling is subject to rescission.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.23(f)(1) excludes residential mortgage transactions used to acquire or build the principal dwelling.
explanations.c: Wrong — cash-out refinances on the principal residence retain the right of rescission.
explanations.d: Wrong — HELOCs on the principal dwelling are subject to rescission.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: HOEPA designates certain loans as 'high-cost' based on the APR exceeding the average prime offer rate (APOR) by specified margins. A high-cost loan must satisfy heightened restrictions. For a first-lien transaction, HOEPA's APR trigger is met when the APR exceeds APOR by more than:

answers.text: More than 1.5 points above APOR
More than 2.5 points above APOR
More than 6.5 points above APOR
More than 3.5 points above APOR

explanations.a: Wrong — 1.5 points is the HPML first-lien spread, not HOEPA.
explanations.b: Wrong — 2.5 points is the HPML jumbo first-lien spread.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.32(a)(1)(i) sets the first-lien HOEPA APR trigger at APR exceeding APOR by more than 6.5 percentage points (with a small-loan adjustment).
explanations.d: Wrong — 3.5 points is the HPML subordinate-lien spread, not HOEPA's trigger.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: HOEPA also designates loans as high-cost when total points and fees cross a threshold relative to the loan amount. The threshold scales for small loans. For a transaction of $20,000 or more, HOEPA's points-and-fees trigger is met when total points and fees exceed:

answers.text: 10% of the total loan amount
5% of the total loan amount
8% of the total loan amount
6% of the total loan amount

explanations.a: Wrong — 10% is not the threshold for loans of $20,000 or more.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.32(a)(1)(ii) sets the threshold at 5% of the total loan amount for loans of $20,000 or more (the dollar threshold adjusts annually).
explanations.c: Wrong — 8% applies to small loans below the dollar threshold.
explanations.d: Wrong — 6% is not the HOEPA points-and-fees threshold.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: A higher-priced mortgage loan (HPML) is defined under Regulation Z by an APR spread above APOR that is lower than HOEPA's high-cost threshold. HPML status triggers escrow and appraisal rules. For a conforming first-lien HPML, the APR exceeds APOR by more than:

answers.text: 1.0 percentage point
2.5 percentage points
3.5 percentage points
1.5 percentage points

explanations.a: Wrong — 1.0 point is below the regulatory spread for HPML status.
explanations.b: Wrong — 2.5 points is the HPML jumbo first-lien threshold, not conforming.
explanations.c: Wrong — 3.5 points is the HPML subordinate-lien threshold.
explanations.d: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.35(a)(1)(i) sets the conforming first-lien HPML threshold at more than 1.5 percentage points above APOR.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Loans classified as HPMLs trigger an escrow requirement for property taxes and insurance. The rule protects borrowers in higher-cost loans from default risk caused by uncollected charges. A creditor must establish and maintain an escrow account on a first-lien HPML for at least:

answers.text: 5 years after consummation
1 year after consummation
3 years after consummation
The full amortization term of the loan

explanations.a: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.35(b) generally requires escrow for at least 5 years on first-lien HPMLs (longer in some circumstances).
explanations.b: Wrong — 1 year is shorter than the regulatory minimum.
explanations.c: Wrong — 3 years does not meet the 5-year minimum.
explanations.d: Wrong — the rule sets a minimum 5-year period, not the full term.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Regulation Z restricts how a loan originator may be compensated to prevent steering borrowers into higher-cost loans. The rule applies to compensation paid by both consumers and other parties. Loan originator compensation may NOT be based on:

answers.text: The total dollar volume of loans the originator closes in a year
Whether the loan closes on schedule for the consumer
A term of the transaction, such as the interest rate, loan type, or LTV
The geographic region in which loans are originated

explanations.a: Wrong — annual loan-volume bonuses are permitted under conditions of 12 CFR 1026.36(d)(1)(iii).
explanations.b: Wrong — closing on schedule is not a transaction term that triggers the rule.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.36(d)(1) prohibits compensation based on a transaction term or proxy for a transaction term.
explanations.d: Wrong — geography is not a transaction term.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Regulation Z's loan originator compensation rule restricts who may pay the originator on a single transaction. The dual compensation prohibition closes a major loophole in the steering protections. If a loan originator receives compensation directly from the consumer, the originator generally:

answers.text: May still receive compensation from the lender, as long as it is disclosed
May receive compensation from the seller of the property
May NOT also receive compensation from any other person in connection with the same transaction
May receive compensation from a title agent or settlement provider

explanations.a: Wrong — disclosure does not cure the dual-compensation prohibition.
explanations.b: Wrong — seller-paid origination compensation is not permitted on top of consumer-paid compensation in the same transaction.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.36(d)(2) bars receiving compensation from any other person on a transaction where the originator receives consumer-paid compensation.
explanations.d: Wrong — third-party settlement providers cannot pay the originator separately under 1026.36(d)(2).

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Regulation Z's coverage of mortgage transactions hinges on the definition of 'dwelling.' The term is broader than many consumers expect. Under Regulation Z, a 'dwelling' includes:

answers.text: A residential structure containing one to four units, including individual condominium units, mobile homes, and trailers used as residences
Only single-family detached homes used as primary residences
Only structures attached permanently to real property
Vacant land held for future residential development

explanations.a: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.2(a)(19) defines 'dwelling' to include 1-4 unit residential structures, individual condominium units, and mobile homes/trailers used as residences.
explanations.b: Wrong — single-family detached structures are not the only dwellings under Regulation Z.
explanations.c: Wrong — mobile homes and trailers used as residences qualify even when not permanently attached.
explanations.d: Wrong — vacant land does not include a residential structure and is not a dwelling.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: TRID combined two prior disclosure regimes into a single, integrated set of forms. The 'Know Before You Owe' initiative was meant to make mortgage shopping clearer for consumers. The purpose of TRID is to:

answers.text: Replace the right of rescission with a single 5-day waiting period
Eliminate APR disclosures on mortgage loans
Standardize underwriting guidelines across all federal mortgage programs
Combine TILA and RESPA disclosures into integrated Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure forms

explanations.a: Wrong — TRID does not change rescission rights.
explanations.b: Wrong — APR disclosure remains required and is shown on the LE and CD.
explanations.c: Wrong — TRID is a disclosure rule, not an underwriting standard.
explanations.d: Correct — TRID integrates the prior GFE/early TIL into the LE and the HUD-1/final TIL into the CD.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Under TRID, an 'application' is defined by six specific pieces of information from the consumer. Receipt of all six starts the clock for issuing the Loan Estimate. The six items are name, income, Social Security number, property address, estimated property value, and:

answers.text: The borrower's monthly debt obligations
The mortgage loan amount sought
The borrower's intended down payment
The borrower's two most recent W-2 forms

explanations.a: Wrong — DTI inputs are needed for underwriting but are not part of the 6-piece application definition.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.2(a)(3) defines application by these six items, the sixth being the loan amount sought.
explanations.c: Wrong — down payment is not one of the six.
explanations.d: Wrong — W-2 forms are verification documents, not part of the definition.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: After receiving an application, the creditor must deliver or place in the mail the Loan Estimate within a specified period. The timing rule starts the consumer's shopping window. The Loan Estimate must be delivered or placed in the mail no later than:

answers.text: The third business day after receipt of the application
The third calendar day after receipt of the application
The seventh business day after receipt of the application
Immediately upon initial inquiry, before any application is taken

explanations.a: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(1)(iii) sets the deadline at the third business day after receipt of the application.
explanations.b: Wrong — the rule uses business days, not calendar days.
explanations.c: Wrong — 7 business days is the minimum lead time before consummation, not the LE delivery deadline.
explanations.d: Wrong — no LE is required at inquiry stage; an application is required first.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: The Closing Disclosure must reach the consumer with enough lead time to review final terms. The waiting period gives consumers a chance to identify problems before closing. The Closing Disclosure must be received by the consumer:

answers.text: At least 7 business days before consummation
At least 3 business days before consummation
On the day of consummation
Within 3 business days after consummation

explanations.a: Wrong — 7 business days is the LE-to-consummation lead time, not the CD-to-consummation rule.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(f)(1)(ii) requires CD receipt at least 3 business days before consummation.
explanations.c: Wrong — same-day delivery defeats the waiting period.
explanations.d: Wrong — the CD must precede consummation, not follow it.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: For purchase-money transactions covered by TRID, the creditor must provide an informational booklet to help consumers understand mortgage costs and processes. The booklet's distribution timing matches the LE deadline. The booklet that must be provided is:

answers.text: The CFPB Mortgage Servicing Handbook
The HUD-1 Settlement Statement guide
The CFPB special information booklet titled Your Home Loan Toolkit
The Fannie Mae Selling Guide summary

explanations.a: Wrong — there is no required servicing handbook delivery at application.
explanations.b: Wrong — the HUD-1 guide is obsolete under TRID.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(g) requires delivery of the CFPB special information booklet, currently titled Your Home Loan Toolkit.
explanations.d: Wrong — the Selling Guide is for lenders, not consumers.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: TRID applies to most closed-end consumer credit transactions secured by real property. Several loan types are excluded from TRID coverage by Regulation Z. TRID does NOT apply to:

answers.text: A 30-year fixed-rate purchase loan on a single-family home
A cash-out refinance on a 1-4 unit owner-occupied dwelling
A construction-to-permanent loan with a single closing
A home equity line of credit secured by the consumer's dwelling

explanations.a: Wrong — standard purchase loans on residential property are TRID-covered.
explanations.b: Wrong — refinances on residential property are TRID-covered.
explanations.c: Wrong — single-closing construction-to-permanent loans are within TRID.
explanations.d: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(1)(i) excludes HELOCs (along with reverse mortgages and certain mobile-home loans) from the LE/CD scheme.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Regulation Z permits a creditor to issue a revised Loan Estimate following certain triggering events. The revised LE may reset tolerance baselines for affected charges. The creditor must deliver or place in the mail a revised Loan Estimate no later than:

answers.text: Seven business days after receiving information establishing the changed circumstance
Three business days after receiving information establishing the changed circumstance
The day before consummation
Within 30 days of the original Loan Estimate

explanations.a: Wrong — 7 business days is not the revised-LE deadline.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(4) requires delivery within 3 business days of receiving information establishing the changed circumstance.
explanations.c: Wrong — waiting until the day before consummation may violate the 4-business-day rule before consummation.
explanations.d: Wrong — the rule is event-triggered, not time-triggered.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Most changes between the initial CD and consummation do NOT require a new three-business-day waiting period. Three specific changes do require a new corrected CD with a new waiting period. Which of the following requires a new three-business-day waiting period?

answers.text: A $200 increase in the recording fee disclosed on the CD
A change in cash to close that does not affect the APR
A change in APR that exceeds 1/8 of 1 percentage point on a fixed-rate loan
A correction of a typographical error in the borrower's name

explanations.a: Wrong — small fee changes alone do not trigger a new waiting period.
explanations.b: Wrong — cash-to-close changes that don't affect APR or product type do not trigger a new period.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(f)(2)(ii) requires a new 3-business-day waiting period for an APR change above tolerance, a loan-product change, or addition of a prepayment penalty.
explanations.d: Wrong — clerical corrections do not trigger a new waiting period.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: TRID assigns charges to one of three tolerance categories. The zero-tolerance category is the strictest because the consumer cannot be charged more at closing than disclosed on the LE. Which of the following is a zero-tolerance charge?

answers.text: Fees paid to the creditor or to a creditor-affiliated provider, and transfer taxes
A title insurance premium when the consumer chose the title company from outside the lender's list
A homeowner's insurance premium chosen by the consumer
Prepaid interest collected at closing

explanations.a: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(3)(i) places creditor and creditor-affiliate fees, fees for services the consumer cannot shop for, and transfer taxes in the zero-tolerance bucket.
explanations.b: Wrong — services the consumer shops for off-list move to the unlimited-variance category.
explanations.c: Wrong — homeowner's insurance is in the unlimited-variance bucket.
explanations.d: Wrong — prepaid interest is unlimited variance, not zero tolerance.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: TRID's 10% tolerance category covers third-party services for which the consumer can shop, when the consumer chooses a provider from the creditor's written list. The aggregate of these charges may not exceed the disclosed amount by more than 10%. Which of the following falls within the 10% tolerance category?

answers.text: Lender origination charges
Per diem prepaid interest
Property taxes paid to the local taxing authority
Recording fees and charges for third-party services where the consumer selected a provider on the creditor's written list

explanations.a: Wrong — lender origination charges are zero-tolerance.
explanations.b: Wrong — prepaid interest is unlimited-variance.
explanations.c: Wrong — property taxes are unlimited-variance.
explanations.d: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(3)(ii) places recording fees and shopped-for-on-list services in the aggregate 10% tolerance bucket.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: After delivery of a Loan Estimate, the disclosed settlement charges generally remain available to the consumer for a limited shopping period. After this period, the creditor may revise the figures without a changed circumstance. The Loan Estimate's settlement charges must remain available to the consumer for at least:

answers.text: 30 calendar days from delivery of the LE
Until the consumer indicates intent to proceed
7 calendar days from delivery of the LE
10 business days from delivery of the LE

explanations.a: Wrong — 30 calendar days is not the regulatory minimum.
explanations.b: Wrong — intent to proceed locks in fees, but the LE itself is offered for at least 10 business days.
explanations.c: Wrong — calendar days is not the unit used by the rule.
explanations.d: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(3)(iv)(E) requires the creditor to honor LE estimates for at least 10 business days, after which a revised LE may be issued.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: The integrated disclosure scheme requires sequential delivery of the LE before the CD. Skipping the LE or replacing it with the CD violates Regulation Z. A creditor may NOT:

answers.text: Deliver the CD before delivering the LE
Deliver the LE and the CD on the same day, with the LE first
Issue a revised LE following a documented changed circumstance
Deliver the LE three business days after receiving the application

explanations.a: Correct — Regulation Z requires the LE before the CD; skipping the LE step violates 12 CFR 1026.19(e) and (f).
explanations.b: Wrong — same-day delivery is permissible if LE precedes CD; sequencing controls.
explanations.c: Wrong — issuing a revised LE for a documented changed circumstance is permitted under 1026.19(e)(3)(iv).
explanations.d: Wrong — that timing meets the LE-delivery deadline.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: TRID's CD timing rule centers on the date of 'consummation,' which is not necessarily the same as funding or recording. The definition is governed by state law of contract formation. Consummation under Regulation Z is:

answers.text: The date the loan is funded by the lender to the closing agent
The time at which a consumer becomes contractually obligated on a credit transaction under applicable state law
The date the deed and mortgage are recorded in the public records
The date the property changes possession from seller to buyer

explanations.a: Wrong — funding can occur after consummation depending on state law and rescission.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.2(a)(13) defines consummation as the time when the consumer becomes contractually obligated under state law.
explanations.c: Wrong — recording is a post-closing step and is not consummation.
explanations.d: Wrong — possession is a real-estate concept, not the credit-contract concept that defines consummation.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: When a creditor's actual charges at closing exceed permitted tolerances, Regulation Z requires the creditor to correct the violation by refunding the excess. The creditor has a limited period to cure the overcharge. A creditor must refund the excess to the consumer no later than:

answers.text: 30 days after the consumer files a complaint with the CFPB
30 days after the loan is sold to a secondary-market investor
60 calendar days after consummation
90 calendar days after consummation

explanations.a: Wrong — the cure runs from consummation, not from a complaint.
explanations.b: Wrong — secondary-market sale is irrelevant to the cure deadline.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1026.19(f)(2)(v) provides a 60-calendar-day cure period after consummation for tolerance violations.
explanations.d: Wrong — 90 days exceeds the regulatory cure window.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: HMDA was enacted to give the public and regulators data about mortgage activity. Reporters submit application-level data each year. The primary purpose of the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act is to:

answers.text: Provide data that helps assess whether financial institutions are serving the housing credit needs of their communities
Establish maximum interest rates and origination fees on mortgages
Set qualifying ratios for residential mortgage underwriting
Require lenders to publicly post their daily pricing schedules

explanations.a: Correct — 12 USC 2801 and 12 CFR 1003.1 state the goals of community-needs assessment and fair-lending oversight.
explanations.b: Wrong — HMDA does not cap rates or fees.
explanations.c: Wrong — HMDA does not set underwriting standards.
explanations.d: Wrong — daily pricing posting is not a HMDA requirement.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Covered institutions submit detailed data on covered applications and originations under Regulation C. The submissions support fair-lending analysis. The data submitted under HMDA is collected on the:

answers.text: Mortgage Acts and Practices Register
NMLS Compliance Register
Loan Application Register
Suspicious Activity Register

explanations.a: Wrong — Regulation N's MAP rule has no register.
explanations.b: Wrong — NMLS does not host HMDA data.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1003.4 requires data collection on the Loan Application Register (LAR).
explanations.d: Wrong — SAR filings are BSA/AML, not HMDA.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: The Fair Credit Reporting Act limits when a user may obtain a consumer report. A 'permissible purpose' is required for each pull. Under FCRA, an MLO may obtain a consumer report:

answers.text: Whenever the most recent file pull is older than 90 days, regardless of consumer activity
In connection with a credit transaction the consumer initiated, with a permissible purpose
For any general business decision, even without consumer involvement
To investigate a competitor's pricing strategy

explanations.a: Wrong — file age does not create permissible purpose; consumer-initiated activity or another statutory purpose is required.
explanations.b: Correct — 15 USC 1681b(a)(3)(A) authorizes pulling a consumer report in connection with a credit transaction initiated by the consumer.
explanations.c: Wrong — generic business curiosity is not a permissible purpose under FCRA.
explanations.d: Wrong — competitive intelligence is never a permissible purpose.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: FACTA amended FCRA to add identity-theft protections. The Red Flags rule requires covered entities to spot patterns and practices that signal identity theft. The Red Flags rule requires financial institutions and creditors to:

answers.text: Pull a tri-merge credit report on every applicant
Encrypt all email communications with consumers
Use multifactor authentication for all employee logins
Develop and implement a written identity theft prevention program

explanations.a: Wrong — credit pulls are governed by FCRA permissible-purpose rules, not Red Flags.
explanations.b: Wrong — the rule is risk-based and does not mandate email encryption specifically.
explanations.c: Wrong — MFA may be a control but is not what the rule itself requires.
explanations.d: Correct — 16 CFR 681.1 requires a written identity theft prevention program designed to detect, prevent, and mitigate identity theft.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: FCRA requires a notice to certain consumers when a creditor sets material loan terms based on a credit report and the terms are less favorable than those provided to a substantial proportion of consumers. The notice gives the consumer information to dispute inaccurate items. The risk-based pricing notice must be provided:

answers.text: Within 90 days after consummation, with a copy of the consumer report
At least 30 days before the application is taken
Before consummation, after the credit decision but in time for the consumer to act on the information
Only if the consumer requests it in writing

explanations.a: Wrong — post-consummation delivery is too late.
explanations.b: Wrong — the notice is decision-based, not pre-application.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 CFR 1022.72-.73 require delivery after the credit decision and before consummation so the consumer may act on the information.
explanations.d: Wrong — the notice is required automatically, not on request.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Residential mortgage lenders and originators that meet defined thresholds are required to file Suspicious Activity Reports under the Bank Secrecy Act. SARs flag transactions that may involve money laundering or other illegal activity. A SAR must generally be filed within:

answers.text: 30 calendar days after detecting the suspicious activity
15 calendar days after detecting the suspicious activity
60 business days after detecting the suspicious activity
90 calendar days after detecting the suspicious activity

explanations.a: Correct — 31 CFR 1029.320(b) requires filing a SAR within 30 calendar days of initial detection.
explanations.b: Wrong — 15 days is shorter than the regulatory deadline.
explanations.c: Wrong — the regulation uses calendar days and 30, not 60 business days.
explanations.d: Wrong — 90 days is past the regulatory deadline.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: GLBA requires financial institutions to inform consumers about how nonpublic personal information is collected, shared, and protected. Consumers must be given an opportunity to limit certain sharing. Under GLBA, a financial institution generally must:

answers.text: Obtain written consent before any internal use of consumer information
Provide a privacy notice only at the consumer's written request
Encrypt consumer data only when transmitting it across state lines
Provide a privacy notice and an opt-out for sharing nonpublic personal information with non-affiliated third parties

explanations.a: Wrong — GLBA does not require consent for internal use; it focuses on third-party sharing.
explanations.b: Wrong — privacy notices must be provided at account opening and annually thereafter when applicable, not on request.
explanations.c: Wrong — encryption obligations are not limited to interstate transmission.
explanations.d: Correct — 15 USC 6802 and Regulation P (12 CFR 1016) require a privacy notice and an opt-out for sharing with non-affiliated third parties.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: GLBA's Safeguards Rule complements its privacy notice rules by addressing data security. Covered entities must develop and document a written information security program. The Safeguards Rule requires financial institutions to:

answers.text: Submit a copy of their security program to the CFPB annually
Develop, implement, and maintain a written information security program with administrative, technical, and physical safeguards
Use only on-premises servers for customer data
Outsource information security to a third-party vendor

explanations.a: Wrong — there is no annual filing of the program with the CFPB.
explanations.b: Correct — the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 CFR 314) requires a written information security program covering administrative, technical, and physical safeguards.
explanations.c: Wrong — cloud and third-party hosting are permitted with appropriate safeguards.
explanations.d: Wrong — outsourcing is allowed but not required.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: The Telephone Consumer Protection Act and the National Do-Not-Call rules restrict telemarketing calls to consumers on the registry. Several exceptions allow continued contact. An MLO may telephone a consumer who is on the National Do-Not-Call registry when:

answers.text: The MLO calls only outside of state-defined business hours
The consumer has an established business relationship with the MLO's company within the look-back period
The consumer's number was previously listed in any public directory
The MLO leaves only voicemail messages and never speaks to the consumer

explanations.a: Wrong — calling outside hours violates time-of-day rules and does not cure DNC status.
explanations.b: Correct — under 16 CFR 310.4(b)(1)(iii)(B) and 47 CFR 64.1200, an existing business relationship within the look-back period (typically 18 months for transactions) creates an exception.
explanations.c: Wrong — public-directory listing is not a DNC exception.
explanations.d: Wrong — voicemail-only contact still violates the registry.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: Regulation N regulates advertising of mortgage products to consumers. The rule prohibits material misrepresentations in commercial communications about mortgage credit products. Regulation N is also known as the:

answers.text: Mortgage Servicing Rule
Mortgage Origination Compensation Rule
Mortgage Disclosure Improvement Act
Mortgage Acts and Practices – Advertising Rule

explanations.a: Wrong — the Mortgage Servicing Rule is part of Regulations X and Z.
explanations.b: Wrong — LO compensation is in 12 CFR 1026.36, not Regulation N.
explanations.c: Wrong — MDIA is part of TILA, not Regulation N.
explanations.d: Correct — 12 CFR 1014 is the Mortgage Acts and Practices – Advertising rule, known as Regulation N or the MAP Rule.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: The E-Sign Act gives electronic signatures and records the same legal effect as paper, when consumer consent procedures are followed. A core protection ensures the consumer can actually receive electronic disclosures. Before electronically delivering disclosures otherwise required to be in writing, the creditor must:

answers.text: Obtain the consumer's affirmative consent and a reasonable demonstration that the consumer can access the electronic format
Provide a paper copy of every disclosure within 24 hours of e-delivery
Send a duplicate copy by certified mail
Obtain a notarized written consent

explanations.a: Correct — 15 USC 7001(c) requires affirmative consumer consent and a reasonable demonstration of ability to access the electronic format.
explanations.b: Wrong — duplicate paper delivery is not a precondition to e-delivery.
explanations.c: Wrong — certified mail is not required.
explanations.d: Wrong — notarization is not part of E-Sign consent.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: The USA PATRIOT Act expanded BSA requirements after 2001 to combat terrorist financing and money laundering. A central piece is the Customer Identification Program. The PATRIOT Act requires covered financial institutions to:

answers.text: Block all wire transfers exceeding $10,000
Disclose customer information to any federal agency on request
Verify the identity of customers and maintain records of the verification
Report all loans on residential property valued over $1 million

explanations.a: Wrong — wire transfers over $10,000 are reportable, but blocking all such transfers is not the rule.
explanations.b: Wrong — agency requests are subject to legal process; the PATRIOT Act does not eliminate that.
explanations.c: Correct — 31 USC 5318(l) and CIP rules require institutions to verify customer identity and retain records.
explanations.d: Wrong — that is not a PATRIOT Act provision.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: The Homeowners Protection Act gives borrowers a path to terminate borrower-paid private mortgage insurance on residential mortgage loans secured by their principal residence. Several termination triggers apply. A borrower may request cancellation of PMI when the loan-to-value ratio reaches:

answers.text: 80% based on the original value of the property
78% based on the original value of the property
80% based on a current appraisal
The midpoint of the loan amortization schedule

explanations.a: Correct — 12 USC 4902(a) allows a borrower-requested cancellation when the principal balance reaches 80% of the original value, with conditions.
explanations.b: Wrong — 78% is the automatic-termination threshold, not the request threshold.
explanations.c: Wrong — borrower-request cancellation under HPA uses original value, not current appraisal.
explanations.d: Wrong — the midpoint is the final-termination backstop, not the request threshold.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: HPA also provides for automatic termination of PMI under certain conditions. The threshold differs from the cancellation request threshold. Automatic termination of PMI occurs when the loan-to-value ratio is scheduled to reach:

answers.text: 80% based on the original value, with no other condition required
75% based on a current appraisal
78% based on the original value of the property, provided the borrower is current on payments
70% based on the original value, immediately

explanations.a: Wrong — automatic termination is at 78%, not 80%.
explanations.b: Wrong — current appraisal is not the automatic-termination basis.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 USC 4902(b) requires automatic termination at the date the LTV is scheduled to reach 78% of the original value, provided the borrower is current.
explanations.d: Wrong — 70% is below the regulatory threshold.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: HPA includes a backstop termination requirement that applies even when the LTV-based triggers are not yet met. This 'final termination' rule eliminates indefinite PMI on a slow-paying loan. PMI must be terminated no later than the:

answers.text: 10th anniversary of consummation, regardless of LTV
First day of the month following the midpoint of the loan's amortization period
Date the loan reaches a 75% LTV based on a current appraisal
Date the borrower refinances into a new mortgage

explanations.a: Wrong — the 10-year mark is not the HPA backstop.
explanations.b: Correct — 12 USC 4902(c) requires final termination on the first day of the month after the loan amortization midpoint, if the borrower is current.
explanations.c: Wrong — current appraisal at 75% is not HPA's final-termination test.
explanations.d: Wrong — refinance is one way to remove PMI but is not the HPA-imposed deadline.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act overhauled financial regulation after the 2008 crisis. Among many provisions, it created a new federal agency dedicated to consumer financial protection. Dodd-Frank established the:

answers.text: Federal Housing Finance Agency
Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
Federal Reserve Board
Consumer Financial Protection Bureau

explanations.a: Wrong — FHFA was created in 2008 by HERA, not Dodd-Frank.
explanations.b: Wrong — the OCC was created in 1863.
explanations.c: Wrong — the Federal Reserve was established in 1913.
explanations.d: Correct — Title X of Dodd-Frank created the CFPB in 2010.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: The CFPB enforces and writes regulations for many federal consumer financial laws. Its rule-writing authority covers most major mortgage statutes. The CFPB has primary rule-writing authority over which of the following?

answers.text: The Internal Revenue Code as it applies to the mortgage interest deduction
RESPA, TILA, ECOA, HMDA, and FCRA's consumer-report use provisions
State property and recording laws
The Securities Act of 1933 and the Exchange Act of 1934

explanations.a: Wrong — the IRS administers federal tax law, not the CFPB.
explanations.b: Correct — Dodd-Frank transferred consumer-financial-law rulewriting for these statutes to the CFPB.
explanations.c: Wrong — state property and recording law is set by state legislatures.
explanations.d: Wrong — federal securities laws are administered by the SEC.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: The CFPB supervises certain depository institutions directly based on size. The threshold determines whether a bank reports to the CFPB or its prudential regulator for consumer compliance examinations. The CFPB has primary supervisory authority over insured depository institutions and credit unions with total assets greater than:

answers.text: $10 billion
$1 billion
$50 billion
$100 billion

explanations.a: Correct — 12 USC 5515 gives the CFPB primary consumer-compliance supervision over depositories with more than $10 billion in assets.
explanations.b: Wrong — $1 billion is below the statutory threshold.
explanations.c: Wrong — $50 billion is not the CFPB supervision threshold.
explanations.d: Wrong — $100 billion is not the threshold for CFPB supervision.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: HUD administers federal housing programs and insures mortgages through one of its operating agencies. The agency it operates is central to first-time-buyer financing. The Federal Housing Administration is part of:

answers.text: The Department of the Treasury
The Veterans Administration
The Federal Reserve System
The Department of Housing and Urban Development

explanations.a: Wrong — Treasury houses the OCC and FinCEN, not the FHA.
explanations.b: Wrong — the VA runs VA loan programs, not FHA.
explanations.c: Wrong — the Federal Reserve does not house FHA.
explanations.d: Correct — FHA has been a part of HUD since HUD's creation in 1965.

questions.name: Federal Mortgage-Related Laws
questions.text: In addition to writing rules, the CFPB has enforcement authority over many entities in the mortgage industry. The bureau's enforcement tools include consent orders, civil penalties, and injunctive relief. The CFPB's authority to enforce federal consumer financial law extends to:

answers.text: Only state-chartered banks
Only depository institutions with more than $50 billion in assets
Non-depository mortgage lenders, brokers, and servicers, regardless of asset size
Only mortgage brokers, but not lenders

explanations.a: Wrong — the CFPB's reach is not limited to state-chartered banks.
explanations.b: Wrong — there is no $50 billion limit on CFPB nonbank enforcement authority.
explanations.c: Correct — 12 USC 5514 gives the CFPB direct supervision and enforcement over nonbank mortgage participants regardless of size.
explanations.d: Wrong — the CFPB reaches both nonbank brokers and lenders.
